events.label: petition
events.text: Governor La Gama petitioned the emperor for defensive fortifications.

evidence.quote: Starting in 1529 , Governor La Gama petitioned the emperor on the need to build defensive fortifications

events.text: Construction of the fortress started, using stone.

evidence.quote: It was built between 1533 and 1540 to defend the harbor of San Juan
Construction started in 1533 , with the use of stone
Construction started in 1533 , with the use of stone , and concluded by 1540

events.text: Structure began serving as the governor's residence.

evidence.quote: Yet the structure has served as the governors residence since 1544

events.label: invasion
events.text: Earl of Cumberland attacked San Juan; fortress was among captures by invaders.

evidence.quote: 1598 , George Clifford , Earl of Cumberland , attacked San Juan

events.label: invasion
events.text: Dutch General Hendrick invaded the city and established himself at the fortress.

evidence.quote: 1625 , General Boudewijn Hendrick ( Balduino Enrico ) of the Netherlands invaded the city and established himself at La Fortaleza

events.label: destruction
events.text: Fortress and city set ablaze during the Dutch retreat.

evidence.quote: During the Dutch retreat , the fortress and the city were set ablaze .

events.text: Reconstruction; chapel of Santa Catalina integrated into the walls.

evidence.quote: During the 1640 reconstruction , the chapel of Santa Catalina , which originally stood outside the walls

events.text: Traditional status as the executive mansion was made official.

evidence.quote: On November 27 , 1822 , its traditional status as the executive mansion was made official

events.text: Massive reconstruction changed military look into a palatial facade.

evidence.quote: The fortress underwent a massive reconstruction in 1846

events.label: tradition
events.text: Last Spanish governor stopped a clock with his sword, marking Spain's loss of the island.

evidence.quote: According to tradition , in 1898 , just before the United States invaded Puerto Rico

events.label: attack
events.text: Nationalist attempt to enter the fortress; four nationalists killed in shootout.

evidence.quote: On October 30 , 1950 , there was an attempt by a few nationalists to enter La Fortaleza

events.label: heritage
events.text: Designated a United States National Historic Landmark.

evidence.quote: On October 9 , 1960 , La Fortaleza was designated a United States National Historic Landmark

events.label: visit
events.text: President John F. Kennedy and Jacqueline Kennedy stayed at the fortress.

evidence.quote: has hosted various dignitaries , including President John F . Kennedy and his wife Jacqueline Kennedy who stayed
in La Fortaleza in 1961

events.label: heritage
events.text: Declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site with San Juan National Historic Site.

evidence.quote: In 1983 , La Fortaleza , along with the San Juan National Historic Site , was declared a World Heritage Site by UNESCO
It was listed by UNESCO in 1983 as part of the World Heritage Site

events.label: incident
events.text: Armed man entered the mailroom and took a receptionist hostage; standoff ended.

evidence.quote: On May 26 , 2004 , a man armed with a knife entered the mansions mailroom

events.label: visit
events.text: U.S. President Barack Obama visited the mansion on a brief trip.

evidence.quote: In June 2011 , U.S . President Barack Obama visited the mansion

events.label: visit
events.text: King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia of Spain visited the fortress.

evidence.quote: King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia of Spain also visited La Fortaleza in 2016

events.label: protest
events.text: Protests around the fortress during Telegramgate, lasting until July 24.

evidence.quote: From July 13 to July 24 , 2019 , the surrounding streets around La Fortaleza were the scene of various protests
